why: A group of size consecutive tiles alternates exactly when all size-1 neighbouring pairs inside it differ. Mark each neighbouring pair on the circle with 1 if they differ, then slide a fixed window of size-1 marks around the circle and count windows that are all 1s.
hints: Instead of checking tiles, look at the edges between neighbours: is tile i different from tile i+1?
A group starting at i alternates iff the size-1 edges after it are all 'different'. That is a fixed-length window over the circular edge array.
Build diff[i] = (t[i] != t[(i+1) % n]), keep a running window sum with indexes taken mod n, and count the n start positions where the sum equals size-1. O(n).
pitfalls: The circle wraps: the last and first tiles are neighbours, and groups may wrap around.
size = 1: every tile is a valid group, answer n.
size = n: the window covers all edges but one; with an odd n a full circle can never alternate.
